source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

06091.t:
Sierra County barely moved in the race for governor. Hilton (R) carried it 929 to 570 over Becerra (D), a margin of 24 points, almost exactly Trump's 24-point margin in 2024. The shift toward the Democrats rounds to zero, while California as a whole moved 10 points their way and the typical county in the state moved 6. Sierra ranks 54th of California's 58 counties by move and 57th by votes cast. Similar Republican-leaning counties moved further: Colusa by 17 points, Yuba by 10 and Mariposa by 3.

Turnout was 1,499 votes, 85% of the 1,754 cast in 2024. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. With 99% of the expected vote counted, these figures are close to final.

06041.t:
In the governor's race, Marin County voted for Becerra over Hilton by 60 points, 99,748 votes to 24,869. That is still a landslide, but it is 4 points less Democratic than Harris's 64-point margin in 2024. That made Marin the only county among California's 58 that moved furthest toward the Republicans. Only three counties in the state moved right at all, while the typical one moved 7 points left and the state as a whole moved 11 points left.

Similar counties went the other way: San Francisco moved 5 points left, Santa Cruz 4 and Alameda 8. Turnout was 86% of the 2024 vote, with 124,617 ballots cast, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06009.t:
In the governor's race, Calaveras County stayed firmly Republican and barely shifted. Hilton beat Becerra here 13,577 to 7,736, a 27-point margin, against Trump's 28-point win in 2024: a move of about 1 point toward the Democrats. Statewide the race swung 11 points left, and the typical California county moved 6 points; Calaveras ranks 51st of 58. Counties of similar size and lean split: Amador hardly moved, while Yuba and Sutter shifted 12 and 17 points left. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Turnout was 21,313 votes, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the small shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from those who stayed home.

06107.t:
Tulare County swung 21 points toward the Democrats in the race for governor, going from a 21-point Trump win in 2024 to a dead heat: Becerra led Hilton by 46 votes, 58,183 to 58,137, out of 116,320 cast. That flips the county from Trump to the Democrat, one of 12 California counties to do so. Its move ranks fifth of the state's 58, against a typical shift of 6 points statewide and 14 nationally.

Turnout was 84% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Counties of similar size and 2024 lean moved much the same way: Kern swung 22 points to a narrow Democratic lead, while Madera and Kings swung 17 and 19 but stayed Republican.

06017.t:
In the governor's race between Becerra and Hilton, El Dorado County went Republican by 13 points, 53,032 votes to 40,798, slightly wider than Trump's 12-point margin over Harris in 2024. That one-point move toward the Republicans set it against the tide. Becerra won the state by 32 points, 54 of California's 58 counties moved left, and only one moved further right than El Dorado.

Comparable counties moved the other way: Placer shifted 3 points left, while Stanislaus and Tulare each swung about 17 to 19 points left. Turnout was 93,830, or 84% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06087.t:
Santa Cruz County voted for Becerra over Hilton for governor by 58 points, 90,275 to 23,799. That is 4 points more Democratic than its 54-point margin for Harris over Trump in 2024. The shift was smaller than the state's 11-point move, smaller than the typical California county's 6 points, and well short of the national typical move of 14. It ranks 38th of 58 counties in the state by move.

Among similar counties, Alameda moved 8 points and Sonoma 5, while San Mateo barely changed. About 114,000 votes were cast, 85% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06023.t:
In the race for governor, Humboldt County gave Becerra (D) 35,162 votes to Hilton's (R) 16,936, a Democratic margin of 35 points. That is up from 28 points for Harris in 2024, a shift of 7 points toward the Democrats. The move sits mid-pack in California, 28th of 58 counties and close to the typical county's 6. It was smaller than the statewide swing of 11 points and the national typical move of 14. Similar counties moved alike: Mendocino and Santa Barbara by about 6, Monterey by 12.

About 52,098 votes were cast, 81% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06051.t:
In the governor's race, Mono County backed Becerra over Hilton by 22 points, 3,015 votes to 1,908, up from Harris's 20-point margin over Trump in 2024. That 2-point shift toward the Democrats is smaller than California's statewide move of 10 points and the typical county's 6, ranking Mono 47th of 58 counties. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Among similar California counties, San Benito moved 9 points and Mendocino 12, while Humboldt moved 4. Mono cast 4,923 votes, 81% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06065.t:
Riverside County swung hard to the Democrats in the race for governor. Becerra beat Hilton here by about 17 points, 445,189 votes to 312,840, in a county Trump carried by 1 point in 2024. That is a move of about 19 points to the left, more than the statewide shift of 11 and well above the typical California county's 7. It ranks seventh of 58 counties by move and was one of 12 to flip from Trump to the Democrat. Neighbouring San Bernardino moved slightly more (21 points), San Joaquin about the same (18), and Orange far less (8).

About 758,029 votes were cast, 81% of the 2024 total. With that drop, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06071.t:
San Bernardino County swung hard toward the Democrats in the race for governor. Trump carried it by 2 points in 2024; Becerra won it over Hilton by 19, 362,375 votes to 248,239. That 21-point move is the third-largest of California's 58 counties, against a typical county move of 6 points and a statewide shift of 11. The county was one of 10 in the state to go from Trump to the Democrat. Its closest neighbours in size and 2024 vote, Riverside and San Joaquin, each moved 17 points, while Orange moved 6.

Turnout fell to 610,614 votes, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06043.t:
Mariposa County moved about 3 points toward the Democrats in the race for governor, but Hilton still carried it comfortably over Becerra, 4,526 votes to 3,137, a Republican margin of 18 points. In 2024 Trump won it by 21 points.

That shift was smaller than in most of California, where 54 of 58 counties moved left and the typical county moved about 6 points. Statewide the swing was 10 points. Mariposa ranks 44th by move. It tracked Plumas (3 points) and Siskiyou (2) but lagged Del Norte (8). Turnout was 81% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06073.t:
San Diego County voted for Becerra over Hilton in the governor's race by 25 points, 751,199 to 448,688. In 2024 Harris carried it by 17, so the county moved 8 points toward the Democrats. That beats the typical California county's 6-point shift and ranks 22nd of 58, but it trails the statewide move of 11 and the national typical move of 14. Comparable counties moved about as much: Orange and Ventura by 8, Sacramento by 10.

Turnout fell to 81% of the 2024 vote, with 1,199,887 ballots counted. That drop is large enough that the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06089.t:
In the governor's race between Becerra and Hilton, Shasta County stayed firmly Republican, voting R+33 after giving Trump an R+37 margin in 2024. Hilton led 44,600 to 22,407. That 3-point move toward the Democrats is about half the typical California county's shift of 6 points, ranking 41st of 58. It is also well short of the state's 11-point swing and the typical national move of 14. Similar counties moved further: Sutter by 19 points, Glenn by 7 and Tehama by 6.

Turnout was 75% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 84% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

06055.t:
In the governor's race, Napa County voted for Becerra over Hilton by 40 points, 38,615 to 16,649. That is 5 points more Democratic than Harris's 35-point margin in 2024. The shift was smaller than California's statewide move of 11 points toward the Democrats and slightly below the typical California county's 6. Napa ranks 34th of 58 counties by move. Similar counties moved further: Yolo by 9 points, Humboldt by 7 and Monterey by 12.

Turnout fell. Voters cast 55,264 ballots, 84% of the 65,549 cast in 2024. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from people changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.

06037.t:
Los Angeles County gave Democrat Becerra a 46-point win over Republican Hilton in the governor's race, 2,229,512 votes to 817,323. That is a 13-point move toward the Democrats from Harris's 33-point margin in 2024, larger than the state's 11-point shift and more than double the typical California county's 6 points. It ranks 14th of 58 counties by move and first by votes cast. Similar large Democratic counties moved less: Contra Costa by 5 points, Santa Clara by 2. Monterey moved 10.

About 3,046,835 votes were cast, 82% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06113.t:
In the race for California governor, Yolo County gave Democrat Becerra 57,529 votes to Republican Hilton's 21,496, a 46-point margin, up from Harris's 36-point margin in 2024. That 9-point move toward the Democrats is larger than the typical California county's (6 points) and ranks 20th of 58 in the state. It is smaller than the 11-point statewide shift and the 14-point typical move nationally. Among similar counties, Yolo moved more than Napa and Contra Costa (5 points each) but less than Monterey (12).

Turnout was 79,025, or 85% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06059.t:
Orange County moved about 8 points toward the Democrats in the governor's race between Becerra and Hilton. Harris carried it by 3 points in 2024. Becerra won it by about 11, 633,955 votes to 511,845. That shift is smaller than California's 11-point statewide swing but larger than the typical California county's 6. It ranks 24th of 58 counties by size of move and third by votes cast. Comparable counties that were close in 2024 swung much harder: Riverside moved 18 points, San Bernardino 21 and San Joaquin 17.

Turnout was 82% of the 2024 total, 1,145,800 votes against 1,390,965. With that drop, the count cannot tell how much of the move came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters staying home.

06033.t:
Lake County flipped in the race for governor. Trump carried it by 1 point in 2024; this time Becerra (D) beat Hilton (R) here by 7, 11,239 votes to 9,803, a move of 8 points toward the Democrats. That is somewhat more than the typical California county's 6-point shift, ranking 24th of 58, but less than the state's 11-point swing and the typical national move of 14.

About 21,042 votes were cast, 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among counties with a similar 2024 result and size, Inyo moved about as much (8 points), Butte less (3) and Imperial far more (31).

06111.t:
In the race for governor, Ventura County voted for Becerra over Hilton by 24 points, 202,078 votes to 124,689. That is 9 points more Democratic than its 15-point margin for Harris in 2024. The shift is larger than the typical California county's 6 points, ranking 21st of 58, but smaller than the state's 11-point move and the 14-point national typical.

Turnout was 326,767 votes, 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among comparable counties, Ventura moved about as much as San Diego (9 points) and Sacramento (10), and far more than San Luis Obispo (2).

06115.t:
Yuba County still voted Republican for governor, but by far less than it did for president. Hilton beat Becerra here 13,469 to 10,382, a 13-point margin, down from Trump's 26-point win in 2024. That 13-point move toward the Democrats ranks 15th of California's 58 counties and roughly doubles the typical county's shift of 6 points. It is a little below the typical national move of 14 points. Becerra won statewide by 31.

Turnout fell to 79% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Yuba stood out among counties with similar 2024 margins and size. Calaveras, Amador and Tuolumne each moved 3 points or less.

06105.t:
Trinity County stayed Republican in the race for governor but by less than in 2024. Hilton led Becerra 2,489 to 2,217, a margin of 6 points, after Trump carried the county by 9. That is a 4-point move toward the Democrats, smaller than the typical California county's 6 and well below the national typical move of 14. It ranks 40th of 58 in the state by move.

About 4,706 votes were cast, 83% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar small counties, Inyo moved 9 points and flipped to the Democrats, Del Norte moved 6, and Plumas moved 2.

06035.t:
In the race for California governor, Lassen County stayed one of the state's most Republican places. Hilton beat Becerra 6,803 to 2,086, a margin of 53 points, nearly matching Trump's 54-point win here in 2024. That one-point shift toward the Democrats ranks 50th of California's 58 counties. The state moved 11 points left, the typical California county 6 and the typical county nationally 14. Among similar counties, Modoc barely moved, while Tehama shifted 5 points left and Glenn 7.

Lassen cast 8,889 votes, about 78% of its 2024 total of 11,371, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06067.t:
In the race for California governor, Sacramento County voted for Becerra over Hilton by 30 points, 358,918 to 192,904. Harris had carried it by 20 points in 2024, so the county moved 10 points toward the Democrats. That is close to the statewide shift of 11 and larger than the typical California county's 6. It ranks 18th of 58 counties by move and 8th by votes cast. Similar Democratic-leaning counties moved slightly less: San Diego and Ventura each about 9 points, Solano 8.

The county cast 551,822 votes, 84% of its 2024 total. The count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06013.t:
In the race for governor, Contra Costa County voted for Democrat Becerra over Republican Hilton by 43 points, 306,285 votes to 122,350. That is 5 points more Democratic than Harris's 38-point margin here in 2024. The move was smaller than the state's 11-point swing toward Becerra and a little below the typical California county's 6 points, ranking 34th of 58. It landed between nearby large Democratic counties: Santa Clara moved 3 points, Sonoma 5 and Yolo 9.

About 428,600 votes were cast, 81% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06097.t:
Sonoma County moved about 4 points toward the Democrats in the race for governor. Becerra beat Hilton 160,705 to 53,005, a margin of about 50 points, up from Harris's 46-point margin over Trump in 2024. That shift was smaller than California's 11-point statewide swing and the typical California county's 6 points, ranking 37th of 58. It was in line with similar Democratic-leaning counties: Santa Cruz moved 4 points, Santa Clara 4 and San Mateo 1.

Turnout was lower than in 2024. The 213,710 votes cast were 85% of the 2024 total of 251,426, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06081.t:
San Mateo County gave Becerra a 51-point win over Hilton in the governor's race, 208,736 votes to 67,203. That is about 1 point more Democratic than Harris's 50-point margin in 2024, a far smaller shift than the 11-point move toward the Democrats statewide. The county ranks 50th of 58 in California by move. The typical county moved 6 points left in the state and 14 nationally.

Counties with similar 2024 margins and size moved further: Sonoma and Santa Cruz each about 4 points, Alameda 8. The county cast 275,939 votes, 83% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06063.t:
In the governor's race, Plumas County stayed firmly Republican and moved only slightly toward the Democrats. Hilton beat Becerra 4,877 to 3,625, a margin of 15 points, compared with Trump's 17-point win here in 2024. That 2-point shift ranks 48th of California's 58 counties, well short of the typical county's 6 points, the state's 11-point swing toward Becerra and the 14-point move of the typical county nationally. It tracks similar counties nearby: Mariposa and Siskiyou each moved about 3 points, while Del Norte moved 6.

Turnout was 8,502 votes, 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who switched sides from those who stayed home.

06047.t:
Merced County swung hard toward the Democrats in the race for governor. Trump carried it by 4 points in 2024; this time Becerra beat Hilton by 18, 42,720 votes to 29,970. That 22-point move to the left is the third-largest of California's 58 counties, well beyond the state's 11-point shift and the typical county's 6. It is also one of 12 counties in the state that went from Trump to the Democrat.

About 72,690 votes were cast, 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among counties that voted similarly in 2024, Merced moved further than Fresno (15 points) and Butte (3) but less than Imperial (31).

06103.t:
In the race for governor between Becerra and Hilton, Tehama County stayed firmly Republican but moved about 5 points toward the Democrats. Hilton won 14,328 votes to Becerra's 6,585, a margin of R+37, compared with Trump's R+42 in 2024. Only 20,913 votes were cast, about 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

The shift was smaller than California's typical county move of 6 points and well below the state's 11-point swing. Similar Republican counties moved further: Glenn by 6 points, Shasta by 8 and Sutter by 17. Tehama ranked 33rd of 58 California counties by move.

06101.t:
Sutter County stayed Republican in the race for governor but by far less than in 2024. Hilton beat Becerra 17,617 to 13,733, a margin of 12 points, after Trump carried the county by 31. That 19-point move toward the Democrats ranks sixth of California's 58 counties, nearly three times the typical county's 6-point shift and ahead of the 11-point statewide swing.

Turnout fell to 80% of the 2024 vote, 31,350 ballots against 39,336, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among counties with similar 2024 margins and size, neighboring-sized Yuba moved 12 points left, while Calaveras and Amador barely moved at all.

06069.t:
San Benito County swung 11 points toward the Democrats in the race for California governor. Harris carried it by 13 points in 2024; Becerra won it by 24, taking 14,350 votes to 8,866 for Hilton. That shift matched the state's own 11-point move and ranks 18th of California's 58 counties, ahead of the typical county's 6 points. Counties that voted similarly in 2024 moved less: Nevada and San Luis Obispo shifted about 2 points each, Ventura 8. Nationally, the typical county moved 14.

Turnout fell to 23,216 votes, 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06005.t:
Amador County did not budge. In the race for governor, Hilton beat Becerra here by 28 points, 12,030 votes to 6,792, the same margin by which Trump beat Harris in 2024. It is one of only four California counties that did not move left: it ranks 55th of 58 by move, while the typical county shifted 6 points toward the Democrats and the state as a whole shifted 10.

Among counties of similar size and 2024 vote, Calaveras was also nearly flat, moving 1 point, but Sutter moved 17 points left and Yuba 10. About 18,822 votes were cast in Amador, 84% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06015.t:
In the race for California governor, Del Norte County favored the Republican, Hilton, over the Democrat, Becerra, by 10 points, 4,547 votes to 3,702. That is narrower than Trump's 16-point win over Harris here in 2024, a move of 6 points toward the Democrats. The shift matches the typical California county, ranks 30th of 58, and trails the statewide move of 11 points and the typical national move of 14. It outpaced comparable counties: Plumas, Mariposa and Siskiyou each moved only 2 to 3 points.

Turnout was 8,249 votes, 78% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06031.t:
In the governor's race, Kings County still backed the Republican, Hilton, but by far less than it backed Trump. Hilton took 18,032 votes to 16,489 for Becerra, a margin of under 5 points, down from Trump's 23-point win in 2024. That 19-point move toward the Democrats is the sixth-largest among California's 58 counties, against 6 points for the typical county and 11 statewide. Among similar counties, Madera moved 17 points, Yuba 12 and Tuolumne 3.

Kings cast 34,521 votes, 83% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters who stayed home.

06057.t:
Nevada County moved toward the Democrats in the governor's race, but by less than most of California. Becerra beat Hilton here by 15 points, 29,799 to 22,085, up from Harris's 12-point margin in 2024, a shift of 3 points. The typical California county moved 7 points left, and Nevada County ranks 47th of 58 by move. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points.

Among California counties with a similar 2024 vote, it tracked San Luis Obispo (2 points) more closely than San Benito (11) or Ventura (9). Turnout was 51,884 votes, 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06011.t:
Colusa County still voted Republican for governor, but by much less than it did in 2024. Steve Hilton beat Xavier Becerra here 3,444 to 2,682, a margin of 12 points, after Trump carried the county by 28. That is a 16-point move toward the Democrats, larger than the state's 11-point shift and the typical California county's 6. It ranks 13th of 58 counties by move.

Turnout was 6,126 votes, 87% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among counties with a similar 2024 margin, Colusa resembled Yuba, which moved 13 points, rather than Amador or Calaveras, which barely moved.

06019.t:
Fresno County flipped. Trump carried it by 4 points in 2024, and in the race for governor Becerra (D) beat Hilton (R) by 12, 149,941 votes to 118,626. That 16-point move toward the Democrats is well beyond California's 11-point shift and the typical California county's 6, ranking 12th of 58. It is close to the typical move nationally (14). Fresno was one of 12 California counties to go from Trump to the Democrat.

About 268,567 ballots were cast, 82% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who switched from those who stayed home. Comparable counties split: San Joaquin moved 18 points and Merced 22, while Placer moved only 3 and stayed Republican.

06109.t:
In the race for governor, Tuolumne County stayed with Hilton, the Republican, giving him 13,875 votes to 9,498 for Becerra, the Democrat, a margin of 19 points. Trump carried it by 22 in 2024, so the county moved 3 points toward the Democrats. That is smaller than the state's 10-point shift, the typical California county's 6 or the typical county nationally at 14. Tuolumne ranks 43rd of 58 in the state by move.

There were 23,373 votes cast, 81% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among California counties of similar size and 2024 lean, Madera and Kings each moved 17 points, while Siskiyou moved 2.

06049.t:
Modoc County barely moved. In the race for governor, Hilton beat Becerra here 2,331 to 842, a Republican margin of 47 points, almost exactly Trump's 47-point edge in 2024. The shift was a fraction of a point toward the Republicans, while Becerra carried California by 31 points, 11 better than Harris did. Fifty-four of the state's 58 counties moved left, the typical one by 6 points, and Modoc ranks 55th. Similar rural counties nearby moved more: Lassen by 1 point, Tehama by 5 and Glenn by 7.

Turnout was 3,173 votes, 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell whether anyone changed their mind or whether some voters simply stayed home.

06003.t:
In the race for governor, Alpine County gave Becerra 408 votes to Hilton's 201, a 34-point Democratic margin, up from Harris's 32-point edge in 2024. That 2-point shift left was smaller than in most of California: Alpine ranks 49th of 58 counties by move, against a typical county move of 6 points and a statewide swing of 11. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left. Similar counties also moved modestly, Mono by 3 points and Napa by 5.

Alpine cast the fewest votes of any California county, 609, or 83% of its 2024 total of 738. With turnout down that much, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Nearly all the expected vote is counted.

06061.t:
In the race for California governor, Placer County backed Hilton over Becerra, 102,369 to 91,095, a Republican margin of 6 points. Trump carried it by 9 points in 2024, so the county moved 3 points toward the Democrats. That is well short of the state's 11-point move and the typical California county's 7. Placer ranks 45th of 58 counties by move.

About 82% as many people voted as in 2024, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among comparable counties, Stanislaus and Fresno swung 18 and 16 points and flipped to the Democrats, while El Dorado barely moved. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

06007.t:
In the race for California governor, Butte County went for Becerra over Hilton by 12 votes, 38,927 to 38,915, after backing Trump by 3 points in 2024. That flip came from a 3-point move toward the Democrats, smaller than the typical California county's 6 points and well short of the state's 11-point shift. Butte ranks 43rd of 58 counties by move. Counties with similar 2024 results moved much further: Merced 22 points, Fresno 15 and Imperial 31.

Butte cast 77,842 votes, 82% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

06079.t:
San Luis Obispo County backed Becerra over Hilton in the governor's race by about 13 points, 71,183 to 55,232. Harris carried it by 11 points in 2024, so the county moved 2 points toward the Democrats. That was one of the smallest shifts in California: it ranked 50th of 58 counties by move, while the typical county moved 6 points left and the state as a whole 11. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points.

Turnout was 126,415 votes, 84% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among counties with similar 2024 margins and size, Nevada moved 2 points, Ventura 9 and San Benito 11.

06099.t:
Stanislaus County flipped in the race for governor, backing Becerra over Hilton by 7 points, 82,466 to 72,278, after voting for Trump by 11 points in 2024. That 18-point swing toward the Democrats ranks eighth among California's 58 counties and is nearly three times the typical county's 6-point move. It outpaced the state's 11-point shift and the 14-point national typical move. Stanislaus is one of 11 California counties that went from Trump to the Democrat.

About 154,744 votes were cast, 78% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Fresno swung 15 points to flip, while Placer moved 3 points left and El Dorado moved 1 point right.

06095.t:
In the governor's race, Becerra beat Hilton in Solano County 100,750 to 53,854, a margin of 30 points. Harris had carried it by 23 in 2024, so the county moved 7 points toward the Democrats. That is a little more than the typical California county (6 points) but less than the state as a whole (10) and well short of the typical county nationally (14). It ranks 27th of California's 58 counties by move.

Turnout was 154,604 votes, 81% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Solano moved more than Santa Barbara (5) but less than Sacramento (10) and Monterey (10).

06077.t:
San Joaquin County flipped. Trump carried it by about 1 point in 2024; in the governor's race, Becerra beat Hilton by 17 points, 128,263 votes to 91,059. That is an 18-point move toward the Democrats, ninth-largest of California's 58 counties and well beyond the state's typical county move of 6 points and the statewide shift of 11. It was one of 12 California counties to go from Trump to the Democrat.

Its swing matched those of similar counties: Fresno moved 16 points, Riverside 19 and San Bernardino 21. Turnout was 219,322 votes, 83% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06021.t:
In the governor's race between Becerra and Hilton, Glenn County voted Republican by 28 points, 5,551 to 3,144, down from Trump's 35-point margin in 2024. That 7-point move toward the Democrats puts it in the middle of California's 58 counties, near the state's typical county shift of 6 points but behind the statewide move of 11 and well short of the national typical move of 14. Counties with similar 2024 results split: Shasta moved 8 points, while Sutter and Colusa moved 17 and 16.

Glenn cast 8,695 votes, 83% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.

06039.t:
Madera County stayed Republican in the race for governor but by far less than in 2024. Trump carried it by 21 points; Hilton won it by 4, 24,269 votes to 22,539 for Becerra. That 17-point swing toward the Democrats ranks 8th of California's 58 counties, well beyond the statewide move of 11 points and the typical county's 6.

Neighbors with a similar 2024 vote split two ways: Tulare and Kings each moved 19 points left, while Tuolumne moved only 3. About 46,808 votes were cast, 86% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

06001.t:
In the race for California governor, Alameda County gave Becerra 446,421 votes to Hilton's 105,850, a Democratic margin of 62 points. That is 8 points more Democratic than Harris's 54-point margin here in 2024. The shift is larger than the typical California county's 6 points but smaller than the statewide move of 11 and the typical national move of 14. Among similar counties in the state, San Mateo barely moved, Santa Cruz shifted 4 points and Sonoma 5.

Turnout fell: 552,271 votes were cast, 82% of the 2024 total. The count cannot tell how much of the move came from voters changing their minds and how much from who stayed home.

06025.t:
Imperial County swung harder toward the Democrats than any other county in California. In the race for governor, Becerra beat Hilton here by 30 points, 26,704 votes to 14,252, in a county Trump had carried by 1 point in 2024. That is a 31-point move, nearly three times the state's 11-point shift and well past the typical California county's 6 points. Comparable counties also moved left but by less: Merced 22 points, Lake 13 and Butte 3.

About 40,956 votes were cast, 76% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot separate people who changed their minds from people who stayed home.

06027.t:
Inyo County flipped from Trump to the Democrat in the race for governor. Harris lost it by 3 points in 2024; Becerra carried it over Hilton by 5, 3,836 votes to 3,485. That 8-point move toward the Democrats is a little larger than the typical California county's 6 points, but smaller than the state's 10-point shift and well below the typical 14-point move nationally. Inyo was one of nine California counties to switch from a Trump win to a Democratic one.

Turnout was 82% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among counties with similar 2024 results and size, Lake moved 14 points, Imperial 32 and Trinity 3.

06075.t:
In the race for governor, San Francisco gave Becerra 280,594 votes to Hilton's 50,784, a Democratic margin of 69 points, up from Harris's 65-point margin over Trump in 2024. That shift was smaller than California's 11-point move toward the Democrats and below the typical county in the state, which moved about 6 points; San Francisco ranks 35th of 58. Among similar heavily Democratic counties, Alameda moved 8 points left and Santa Cruz 4, while Marin moved 5 points toward the Republicans.

About 331,378 votes were cast, 82% of the 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06029.t:
Kern County, which Trump carried by 21 points in 2024, narrowly backed Becerra over Hilton for governor, 118,131 to 114,697, a 2-point Democratic margin. The 23-point swing toward the Democrats ranks third among California's 58 counties, about double the statewide move of 11 points and well above the typical California county's 7 and the national typical of 14. Kern is one of 12 California counties that went from Trump to the Democrat.

Among similar counties, Tulare swung 21 points to finish essentially even, while Madera and Kings moved 17 and 19 points but stayed Republican. Kern cast 232,828 votes, 82% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06093.t:
In the governor's race, Siskiyou County stayed firmly Republican: Hilton beat Becerra 10,039 to 7,166, a margin of 17 points. That is 3 points narrower than Trump's 19-point win over Harris in 2024, a small move toward the Democrats. Statewide, Becerra won by 31 points, an 11-point swing left from 2024, and the typical California county moved 6 points. Siskiyou ranked 47th of 58 by move.

Its shift matches similar Republican counties nearby. Tuolumne and Mariposa each moved 3 points, Plumas 2. Turnout was 80% of the 2024 vote, 17,205 ballots against 21,489, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06083.t:
Santa Barbara County backed Becerra over Hilton for governor by 33 points, 103,185 votes to 52,116. Harris carried it by 27 in 2024, so the county moved 6 points toward the Democrats. That is exactly the typical move among California's counties and puts it 29th of 58, but it trails the statewide shift of 11 points and the national typical move of 14. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Solano by 8, Humboldt by 6 and Monterey by 11.

About 155,301 votes were cast, 84% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot show how much of the move came from voters changing their minds and how much from voters who stayed home.

06085.t:
In the governor's race, Santa Clara County voted for Becerra over Hilton 435,779 to 171,780, a Democratic margin of 44 points, up from Harris's 40-point margin over Trump in 2024. That 4-point shift to the left was smaller than the state's 11-point move and the typical California county's 6, ranking 40th of 58. Nationally, the typical county moved 14. Comparable Democratic counties moved a little more: Contra Costa 5 points, Sonoma 4 and Yolo 9.

There were 607,559 votes cast, 81% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Even so, the county cast the sixth-largest vote in the state.

06045.t:
Mendocino County moved toward the Democrats in the governor's race, though by less than California as a whole. Becerra beat Hilton here 21,133 to 10,557, a margin of 33 points, up from Harris's 27-point edge over Trump in 2024. That shift of nearly 7 points put the county at the middle of the state's 58 counties and roughly matched the typical California county, but it trailed the statewide move of 11 points and the national typical move of 14.

Its closest California peers, Humboldt and Santa Barbara, moved by similar amounts, while Monterey shifted about 12 points. About 31,690 votes were cast, 81% of the 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

06053.t:
In the race for governor, Monterey County backed Becerra over Hilton 87,731 to 36,512, a Democratic margin of 41 points. Harris carried it by 30 in 2024, so the county moved 11 points toward the Democrats. That matches the statewide shift of 11 and is larger than the typical California county's move of 6. Monterey ranked 17th of 58 counties by move. Similar counties moved less: Santa Barbara and Humboldt about 6 points each, Solano 8. Nationally, the typical county moved 14.

Turnout was 124,243 votes, 85% of the 2024 total. The count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.
